item.title: From Philosophical Critique to Research Program
item.lead: The dossier does not conclude the foundational layer with a single judgment, but with a program for triangulation: legal documents, technical data, and sociological analysis must mutually support each other.

blocks.text: The source identifies three lines of evidence. The first is legal: contracts, privacy documentation, enforcement dossiers, and consumer law sources. The second is technical: CRM screenshots, IP logs, dashboards, scripts, and other operational artifacts. The third is sociological: patterns in relationship formation, psychological mechanisms, and demographic data. The starting point is that no single line of evidence would be sufficient on its own.

This research architecture is important because the dossier speaks on various levels. Some passages are descriptive and claim that certain workflows exist. Others are interpretive and connect those workflows to psychological or demographic effects. Yet others are normative and formulate what legislation or society should do. The source itself advises against conflating these categories.

A professional research version could therefore use a status label for each core point: source claim, directly documentable, indirectly supported, hypothesis, or normative proposal. This strengthens the dossier without losing its critical perspective.

The foundation of this series is therefore not the assumption that all described mechanisms have already been proven. The foundation is the research question: what happens when human need is measured, profiled, and monetized on the same scale as advertising or e-commerce behavior? This question is broader than a single platform and forms the connecting thread between the seven parts.
